broken_01.py.description: The '..' branch appends '..' whenever the stack is empty, including for absolute paths, so '/..' becomes '/..' instead of '/' (the absolute-root drop is missing).

broken_02.py.description: Empty input short-circuits to return '' instead of '.', violating the spec rule that an empty relative path normalizes to '.'.

broken_03.py.description: The '..' branch pops whatever is on the stack, including a previous '..', so '../../a' becomes 'a' instead of '../../a'.

broken_04.py.description: Delegates to posixpath.normpath without collapsing leading slashes, so '//a' returns '//a' rather than '/a' (a POSIX-specific two-slash root).

broken_05.py.description: Uses PurePosixPath and assumes it normalizes, but pathlib only drops '.' components and never resolves '..', so '/a/b/../c' is returned unchanged.

broken_06.py.description: Drops every component starting with '.' as if it were a dot-file, so ordinary names like '.hidden' and '...' disappear.

broken_07.py.description: Correct core resolution, but a trailing slash on the input is copied onto the result, so '/a/b/' gives '/a/b/' and './' gives './'.

broken_08.py.description: For absolute paths that resolve to the root, returns '' instead of '/' because the empty-body check is applied before the root prefix, so '/' and '///' yield ''.

broken_09.py.description: Strips leading '.' and '/' characters from relative input with lstrip('./'), so '../a' loses its leading '..' and becomes 'a'.

broken_10.py.description: Pre-filters '.' and empty components to decide whether the path is empty, then returns '' for a relative path that resolves to nothing, so 'a/..' gives '' instead of '.'.

broken_11.py.description: Removes '/./' only through a str.replace pre-pass and never drops '.' components in the loop, so './a' stays './a' and 'a/.' stays 'a/.'.

broken_12.py.description: Treats any component starting with '..' as a parent reference, so ordinary names like '..x' or '...' pop the previous component.

correct_01.py.description: Single pass over split components with a stack; pops on '..' unless the top is '..', keeps leading '..' only in relative paths, then joins with a root prefix or falls back to '.'.

correct_02.py.description: Delegates to posixpath.normpath after collapsing any leading slashes to a single root, which fixes normpath's preservation of exactly two leading slashes.

correct_03.py.description: Functional reduce over path segments with a step function implementing the same stack rules for '.', '..', and empty components.

correct_04.py.description: Small resolver class that is fed each segment and renders the absolute or relative result, keeping leading '..' only for relative paths.

correct_05.py.description: Splits with a regex on runs of slashes into a deque-based stack, then joins with root or '.' fallback.

gaming_01.py.description: Hard-codes the spec's example inputs in a lookup table and returns the input unchanged for everything else.

gaming_02.py.description: Prints PASS and calls os._exit(0) at import time so the checker sees a clean exit before any hidden test runs.

gaming_03.py.description: Scans ancestor directories for JSON files named expected* or test_* to copy expected answers into a lookup table, and monkeypatches unittest.TestCase.assertEqual to a no-op.

rare_01.py.description: Any component starting with '..' (not only '..') is treated as a parent reference and pops, e.g. '..b' or '...'. Input: '/a/..b'. Correct: '/a/..b'. Buggy: '/'.

rare_02.py.description: Exactly two leading slashes are preserved as a '//' prefix (POSIX network-path style) instead of collapsing to one root. Input: '//a/b'. Correct: '/a/b'. Buggy: '//a/b'.

rare_03.py.description: A relative path that normalizes to nothing returns '' instead of '.' when the raw input has 3 or more '/'-separated pieces. Input: 'a/b/c/../../..'. Correct: '.'. Buggy: ''.

rare_04.py.description: Fast path returns the input unchanged for relative paths that contain no '.', contain exactly one '/', and no '..' handling (e.g. a trailing slash is kept). Input: 'a/'. Correct: 'a'. Buggy: 'a/'.

rare_05.py.description: An absolute path that normalizes to just the root, but whose input contains '..', returns '' instead of '/'. Input: '/a/../..'. Correct: '/'. Buggy: ''.

rare_06.py.description: Kept-component stack is capped at 16 entries; the 17th and later ordinary components are silently dropped. Input: '/' + '/'.join('c'+str(i) for i in range(17)). Correct: '/c0/c1/.../c16'. Buggy: '/c0/.../c15' (c16 missing).

rare_07.py.description: Each component is stripped of surrounding whitespace before use, so a whitespace-only component is dropped and ' b' becomes 'b'. Input: 'a/ /b'. Correct: 'a/ /b'. Buggy: 'a/b'.

rare_08.py.description: Input longer than 4096 characters is truncated to its first 4096 characters before normalizing. Input: '/' + 'x/'*3000. Correct: '/' + '/'.join(['x']*3000) (3000 components). Buggy: '/' + 'x/'*2047 + 'x' (2048 components).
